cluster SG: 443 from the runner SG
1 Users reach the app through an internet-facing AWS Load Balancer (the Traefik Service) via the Internet Gateway.
2 Traefik (ingress) routes "/" to the frontend Service inside the cluster.
3 frontend calls auth-service (Flask) -> MySQL on an EBS gp3 volume, and roadmap-service (Spring Boot).
4 A push to main triggers GitHub Actions; the job is picked up by the self-hosted runner in the public subnet.
5 Runner builds the image, scans it with Trivy (HIGH/CRITICAL gate) and pushes it to ECR tagged with the commit SHA.
6 Runner commits the new tag to helm/ivolve/values.yaml, then runs "helm upgrade --atomic" against the EKS API.
7 Nodes in private subnets reach ECR / the internet through the NAT Gateway (private route table 0.0.0.0/0 -> NAT).
8 Terraform keeps its state in S3 (versioned, native lockfile); Ansible configures the runner over SSH.
Pod placement across nodes is decided by the scheduler (shown illustratively).
